title: Maximum residue levels for deltamethrin
summary: Deltamethrin MRLs for kiwis, melons, and watermelons will increase from 5 November 2026
update: The European Union (EU) has increased the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for deltamethrin on kiwi fruits, melons, and watermelons. In May 2026 the MRL was increased for cherries.
what_changing: The EU has increased the MRLs for deltamethrin as listed in Table 1.
why: The European Food Safety Authority analysed an application from the producer of deltamethrin to increase the MRLs on kiwis, melons, and watermelons, and concluded that this change poses no risks to consumers ( EFSA 2026 ).
timeline:
The new MRLs for kiwis, melons, and watermelons apply from 5 November 2026 .

The new MRL for cherries applies from 12 May 2026 .
background:
MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database .

The increased MRL for cherries in May 2026 followed an evaluation by EFSA (2025 ). In June 2025, the EU raised the MRL for deltamethrin on papayas from 0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg in line with the Codex MRL (CXL) adopted in 2024.
